title: DeriveBSD UI DataTransfer Grant (v0.1)

subject.description: Exact subject holding this grant. For direction=read this is ordinarily the destination/consumer; for direction=write this is ordinarily the source creating the offer.

offer_source_subject.description: Exact subject that created or exposed the offer. For direction=read this is ordinarily the source/exporting side; for direction=write this ordinarily equals subject.

delivery_mode.description: single-delivery is the baseline for cross-domain workstation transfer; the first successful read-side transfer exhausts the grant and ordinary recovery is a fresh explicit grant / re-offer rather than replay/history resurrection. multi-delivery is an explicit exception lane. Under successor continuity, add/drop/swap is fresh-grant required; reviewed successor continuity keeps delivery_mode exact.

id.description: Offer identifier (clipboard entry / drag offer). Useful as an operational correlate, but not the portable source of truth for renewal continuity or successor scope, and not the portable source of truth for payload lineage or exact payload binding.

payload_digest.description: Optional digest of the exact offered payload for this reviewed transfer story. Under successor continuity, this becomes the portable exact-payload binding; semantic-equivalence rebinding is fresh-grant required.

ttl_seconds.description: Optional relative lifetime hint in seconds. The grant still publishes exact `effective_until`; if both are present, effective_until must be no later than issued_at + ttl_seconds.

redaction_profile_digest.description: Optional digest of redaction.transform artifact. Under successor continuity, successor continuity keeps this exact; add/drop/swap is fresh-grant required.

content_source.description: Optional provenance join for payloads copied from a receipted artifact such as OCR/searchable inspection output. Under successor continuity, successor continuity keeps this exact when present; add/drop/swap is fresh-grant required.

renewal_posture.description: Whether this grant starts a new reviewed transfer story or is the reviewed successor of an earlier transfer grant. Successor continuity is only for the same reviewed transfer story, not for broader actor/scope changes.

supersedes_grant_digest.description: Digest of the prior ui.datatransfer.grant superseded by this renewed/re-offered grant. Renewal stays new-artifact-plus-predecessor-digest, not in-place extension.

successor_scope_posture.description: Required when renewal_posture = supersedes-prior-grant. Declares that successor continuity stays on the same source/destination pair and the same-or-narrower typed offer envelope; broader actor/scope changes are fresh-grant required.

requires_foreground.description: Optional foreground/interactivity requirement. Under successor continuity, add/drop/swap is fresh-grant required; when present in the predecessor, successor continuity keeps this exact.

rate_limit.description: Optional throttling/throughput posture. Under successor continuity, add/drop/swap of constraints.rate_limit is fresh-grant required; when present in the predecessor, successor continuity keeps this exact.

expires_at.description: Optional absolute upper bound. If present, grant effective_until must be no later than this value. Under successor continuity, successor continuity keeps this exact; add/drop/swap of constraints.expires_at is fresh-grant required.

constraints.description: closed-world typed vocabulary for ordinary workstation transfer posture. The baseline typed keys are requires_foreground, rate_limit, and expires_at; future extra posture needs an ADR/spec change rather than hidden extra constraints.* keys.

effective_until.description: ISO8601 time. exact end of ordinary transfer authority for this grant artifact. If offer.ttl_seconds and/or constraints.expires_at are present, effective_until must be no later than those bounds; late delivery fails closed.

description: portable ordinary workstation transfer baseline. This ordinary workstation transfer baseline is frozen at this shape and complete enough to implement; future richer transfer lanes are RFC-first rather than quiet growth of this artifact family. Future richer transfer lanes must mint distinct artifact families instead of widening or variant-switching this ordinary baseline family.
